facts.claim: Oxytocin causes intergroup bias because it motivates in-group favoritism and, to a lesser extent, out-group derogation.
facts.quote: Results show that oxytocin creates intergroup bias because oxytocin motivates in-group favoritism and, to a lesser extent, out-group derogation.

facts.claim: Latino patients gave clinicians lower ratings than did other groups (P <. 0001), and this did not depend on the clinicians' implicit bias (P = . 98).
facts.quote: Latino patients gave the clinicians lower ratings than did other groups (P <. 0001), and this did not depend on the clinicians' implicit bias (P = . 98).

facts.claim: An individual's economic decisions to trust is predicted by that person's bias in implicit race attitude.
facts.quote: We demonstrate that race disparity in both an individual's explicit evaluations of trustworthiness and, more crucially, his or her economic decisions to trust is predicted by that person's bias in implicit race attitude.

facts.claim: Health providers demonstrated negative implicit biases toward women with lower educational attainment when making referrals to multidisciplinary care.
facts.quote: When making referrals to multidisciplinary care, HCPs demonstrated negative implicit biases toward women with lower educational attainment.

facts.claim: Oncologist implicit bias indirectly predicted less patient confidence in recommended treatments, and greater perceived difficulty completing them, through its impact on oncologists' communication.
facts.quote: In addition, oncologist implicit bias indirectly predicted less patient confidence in recommended treatments, and greater perceived difficulty completing them, through its impact on oncologists' communication (as rated by both patients and observers).

research.angle: While implicit biases toward specific groups can influence trust and communication, some patient dissatisfaction is independent of those biases.
research.verdict: The evidence shows that implicit biases significantly shape social and economic trust and influence healthcare interactions, but they do not always account for all patient perceptions.
research.caveat: One study shows that Latino patients' lower ratings of clinicians were not dependent on the clinicians' implicit bias.
